messages:
Priya: ran into a strange one with the async Python SDK. got a 422 but instead of our ValidationError the call bubbled httpx.HTTPStatusError and the errors list vanished. sync client still returns ValidationError.
Dylan: can you paste the raw bytes you received and sdk version?
Priya: sdk 0.12.3. raw body bytes: b'{\n  "error":"validation_failed",\n  "errors":[{"field":"prompt","message":"invalid bytes"},{"field":"meta","message":"caf\\xe9"}]\n}' (note the caf\\xe9 byte).
Ken: sounds like encoding/decoding differences in async path. async may call response.raise_for_status() which triggers httpx to decode text and raise before our parsing helper runs.
Ivy: parity bug. proposal: centralize error normalization so both sync and async use response.content (bytes), decode with utf-8 and errors='replace', then json.loads. If parsing fails, attach raw_body and raise SDKException('malformed error payload'). Also preserve status_code and headers on the SDK exception.
Dylan: typing follow-up: expose ValidationError as typed class with status_code: int, errors: List[Dict[str, Any]], raw_body: str in our stubs so mypy users can rely on attributes.
Priya: current workaround is catching httpx.HTTPStatusError and re-parsing which is awful for onboarding examples.
Ivy: I'll open a PR to adjust async request flow to call _normalize_response(response) before raising, add unit tests using MockTransport returning mixed-encoding bytes, and include a small sample snippet for docs: `async with RedwoodClient() as c:\n    try:\n        await c.responses.create(...)\n    except ValidationError as e:\n        for err in e.errors:\n            print(err['field'], err['message'])`.
CI Bot: please add changelog entry under "client: async error parity + robust decoding" and mark for backport to 0.12.x. :robot_face:
Priya: thanks, will watch the PR. this affects a few enterprise customers with legacy metadata encodings.
Dylan: thanks for catching @Priya, looks like a good small fix.
